problems.quote: `canCraftInDimensions` is the more generous `width >= 3 && height >= 3`, which is the same asymmetry vanilla's recipe carries: a modded grid bigger than 3×3 advertises the recipe but `matches()` still refuses it.
problems.issue: The consequence is wrong. A CraftingInput is never the raw container size: CraftingContainer.asPositionedCraftInput() calls CraftingInput.ofPositioned(), which crops the grid to the bounding box of the non-empty slots (build/neoForm/neoFormJoined1.21.1-20240808.144430/.../world/item/crafting/CraftingInput.java:36-82, .../world/inventory/CraftingContainer.java:15-21). A 3x3 pattern placed anywhere inside a 4x4 or larger modded grid therefore reaches matches() as a 3x3 input and DOES match — that cropping is exactly what makes `>= 3` the right dimension check. matches() only refuses when the filled area itself is not 3x3 (e.g. a stray tenth item outside the block).
problems.correction: Say instead: matches() requires the *filled* area to be exactly 3x3. Because vanilla crops the crafting input to its non-empty bounding box, a 3x3 pattern in a bigger modded grid still matches; only the 2x2 inventory grid, which can never produce a 3x3 input, is out. (The `>= 3` vs `== 3` difference between the two methods is real and is vanilla's, but it does not mean larger grids are refused.)
